title: The birds
hookLine: Francis preaches to the birds, who stay to listen

cards: What would you say to a flock of birds, if you thought they were listening? Shoo, maybe.

Francis is on the road with his companions in the Umbrian countryside when he sees trees by the way filled with birds, and more on the ground. He tells his brothers to wait and walks over, alone, into the middle of them.
They don't scatter. The ones in the trees come down and gather at his feet, waiting. He has an audience, so he preaches.

teach.b: Thomas of Celano, an early biographer, tells this story, and so do the Little Flowers. Francis begins the way he begins with anyone: my little sisters the birds. His sermon isn't a scolding.

teach.h: A SERMON THAT'S A LIST OF GIFTS.
teach.b: It's a list of gifts. You owe a great deal to God your Creator, he tells them, so praise him always. He gave you freedom to fly anywhere, and clothing, feathers twice and three times over.

He kept your kind safe in Noah's ark. He gave you the air, springs and rivers to drink from, mountains and valleys for shelter, tall trees for your nests. And you don't sow or reap, and God feeds you anyway.
That last line is Jesus's own, from the Sermon on the Mount, in the Douay-Rheims: "Behold the birds of the air, for they neither sow, nor do they reap, nor gather into barns."

Francis is reading the gospel back to the ones it was about. The Little Flowers says they open their beaks, stretch out their necks, spread their wings and bow their heads to the ground, as if to show they understood.
They don't leave until he blesses them with the sign of the cross.

teach.h: THEY BOW, THEN FLY OFF IN A CROSS.
teach.b: Then they rise all at once, singing, and fly off north, south, east and west, so the flock makes a cross in the sky. Celano adds a human detail.

teach.h: HE BLAMED HIMSELF FOR BEING LATE.
teach.b: Francis blamed himself for never having preached to birds before, and from then on, the story says, urged every creature he met to praise its Maker.

teach.h: BEHOLD THE BIRDS OF THE AIR.
teach.b: In his eyes the whole creation was singing, and he'd been slow to join in.

how: Catholics remember Francis's sermon to the birds in art and story, and on or near his feast day some parishes hold a blessing of animals in his honor.

practice: Open a window if you can, and listen outward, past the hum of the house and the traffic, and wait for a bird.
When one comes, don't name it; just hear it the way Francis heard his audience, something alive making its own sound, and if none comes, any living sound will do.
If you pray, let that sound be a small praise you join; if you don't, let it be company.
